title: 月之暗面 Kimi K3.1 Pro 上线 OpenRouter，1M 上下文多模态开源权重模型
content:
OpenRouter· @OpenRouter · X·· 5 小时前精选AI 评分77
AI 导读
OpenRouter 宣布月之暗面的 Kimi K3.1 Pro 上线，定位为基于 Kimi K3 后训练、面向长程编码和智能体任务的 1M 上下文多模态开源权重模型。定价为 $2/M input tokens、$10/M output tokens，可在 OpenRouter 直接试用。
推荐理由
OpenRouter 上架页直接给出上下文长度、定价和试用链接，读者可以据此评估这个开源权重模型的使用成本。
正文 · AI 翻译
来自 @Kimi_Moonshot 的 Kimi K3.1 Pro 已在 OpenRouter 上线。
这是一个 1M 上下文、多模态的开源权重模型，基于 Kimi K3 进行后训练，面向长程编程和智能体任务。输入 $2/百万 tokens，输出 $10/百万 tokens。
来源：OpenRouter · x.com

report.summary: Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro — a 1M-context, multimodal open-weight model post-trained for long-horizon coding and agent tasks — launches on OpenRouter at $2/$10 per million tokens.
report.background: Moonshot AI built its reputation on the Kimi assistant and then on open-weight releases, most notably the Kimi K2 series, which let developers run near-frontier models on their own hardware. OpenRouter has meanwhile become the default marketplace for model access: one API key, hundreds of models, per-token pricing and failover across providers. The two trends converge here. Chinese labs — DeepSeek, Qwen, Zhipu, MiniMax — have been shipping open-weight models well below US frontier-lab prices, dragging the whole market downward. Simultaneously, demand has shifted from chat to agents: coding assistants, terminal agents and multi-step workflows need long context, dependable tool calling and predictable cost per task rather than per message. A 1M-token window matters most for repository-scale code, long transcripts and multi-hour agent runs. The "Pro" suffix implies a post-training pass over the K3 base rather than a fresh pretrain — now a standard cadence of shipping cheaper incremental upgrades between major versions.
key_points: The model offers a 1M-token context window, multimodal input and open weights, and is post-trained from Kimi K3 rather than trained from scratch. Moonshot positions it explicitly for long-horizon coding and agentic workflows — workloads where context length, tool-calling reliability and cost per completed task matter more than single-turn benchmark scores.

Pricing on OpenRouter is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output. That places it mid-tier: well above budget open-weight models, far below flagship closed APIs. The 5:1 input/output ratio rewards the long-prompt, short-completion pattern typical of coding agents, but penalises agents that ramble.

Distribution through OpenRouter cuts adoption friction to near zero: developers can test the model with an API key they already have before committing to self-hosting. The marketplace also lets multiple inference providers serve the same weights and compete on price and throughput, which tends to compress effective cost over time.

Open weights mean the checkpoints can be downloaded, fine-tuned and run privately, which matters for regulated industries and teams that cannot send source code to third-party APIs. It also lets the community benchmark the actual model rather than trusting vendor-reported numbers.

The release signals Moonshot's cadence of frequent post-training refreshes instead of waiting for a full generational leap, keeping its models visible on aggregator leaderboards while base-model training continues in the background.
report.impact: For the AI industry this reinforces a pattern: open-weight releases from Chinese labs now set the price floor and the context-length baseline, forcing closed-model vendors to justify premiums on reliability, tooling and safety rather than raw capability. For developers, a 1M-context multimodal model at $2/$10 is a credible default for repository-scale refactoring, log analysis and multi-step agents — worth benchmarking against your current pick on task completion rate rather than token price alone, since long agent runs burn output tokens fast. Open weights also enable self-hosting and domain fine-tuning without data leaving your network. For regular users the effect is indirect but real: cheaper agentic features inside coding tools and consumer apps, and more products shipping long-document and screenshot understanding without passing on flagship-API costs.
report.tools: Start on OpenRouter's playground or its OpenAI-compatible endpoint to price a real workload. For self-hosting, watch vLLM and SGLang for day-one weight support, with LM Studio and Ollama for desktop use. On the agent side, Aider, Cline and Roo Code are the quickest way to test the long-horizon coding claims; LMArena and Artificial Analysis track community rankings and price-performance comparisons.
